topLine: Labor's $6.8 billion pledge to electrify and duplicate the South Coast rail line between Kiama and Bomaderry is the day's biggest development for the region, landing alongside fresh polling that shows One Nation running strongly in NSW. Statewide, the Minns government's last-minute pause on real estate underquoting laws dominated coverage and drew a wave of critical commentary about a pattern of policy reversals before the March election. Two polls — DemosAU and Resolve — both point to a significant One Nation vote.

briefing.topLine: Labor's $6.8 billion pledge to electrify and duplicate the South Coast rail line between Kiama and Bomaderry is the day's biggest development for the region, landing alongside fresh polling that shows One Nation running strongly in NSW. Statewide, the Minns government's last-minute pause on real estate underquoting laws dominated coverage and drew a wave of critical commentary about a pattern of policy reversals before the March election. Two polls — DemosAU and Resolve — both point to a significant One Nation vote.
briefing.localWatch: Labor has promised $6.8 billion to electrify the South Coast line and duplicate track from Kiama to Bomaderry, while the Illawarra Mercury reports One Nation could win up to 27 per cent in strongholds such as Kiama and Shellharbour and the party has named Kiama teacher Daniel Hill on its upper house ticket. Locally, Kiama councillors approved a CBD apartment block that breaches height limits, and Nowra's urgent care clinic has passed 10,000 patient visits.

stories.headline: 'Should have happened years ago': commuters react to massive South Coast trains promise
stories.summary: The Illawarra Mercury reports a $6.8 billion Labor election promise to electrify the South Coast rail line and duplicate tracks between Kiama and Bomaderry, aimed at reducing delays. The paper reports commuter reaction to the pledge.

stories.headline: Surging One Nation vote could mean new 'political reality' in Labor's Illawarra fortress: MPs
stories.summary: The Illawarra Mercury reports One Nation could attract up to 27 per cent of the vote in NSW seats considered Labor strongholds, including Kiama and Shellharbour. The report says party insiders have discussed how to respond, with MPs quoted on a possible new "political reality".

stories.headline: From a family miracle to Macquarie Street: Why Daniel Hill is entering politics
stories.summary: One Nation has named Kiama teacher Daniel Hill on its NSW upper house ticket, the South Coast Register reports. The piece covers his stated reasons for entering politics.

stories.headline: Kiama CBD apartments 'unfortunately' approved by councillors
stories.summary: Kiama councillors approved a proposed apartment block on the town's main street at Tuesday's meeting despite it breaching height limits, the Illawarra Mercury reports.

stories.headline: More doctors, bulk billing and 10,000 visits: What's behind the local surge
stories.summary: The South Coast Register reports Nowra's urgent care clinic has now treated 10,000 patients, amid an influx of regional medical staff. The paper links the increase in doctors and bulk billing to shared hospital resources following the Shoalhaven hospital overhaul.

stories.headline: The 'haunting' Wall of Tears on display at Port Kembla gallery
stories.summary: The Illawarra Mercury reports that a memorial listing the names of 18,457 children killed in Gaza, which it says was banned by Shoalhaven City Council, will instead be displayed at the NASA Gallery in Port Kembla.

stories.headline: DemosAU: Labor 30, Coalition 24, One Nation 22 in New South Wales
stories.summary: A DemosAU state poll reported by The Poll Bludger has primary votes of Labor 30, the Coalition 24 and One Nation 22, with Labor retaining what the site describes as a commanding two-party lead. The report says Chris Minns' lead as preferred premier has narrowed substantially.

stories.headline: The Pauline factor: Why NSW women love One Nation
stories.summary: The Sydney Morning Herald reports that the latest Resolve Political Monitor has One Nation and Labor level among female voters in NSW.

stories.headline: Pauline steps in over gas call
stories.summary: The Daily Telegraph reports that surfers have joined MPs and environmentalists in opposing One Nation's position on the PEP11 offshore gas project.

stories.headline: Students see red: protest breaks out at Pauline Hanson's Toronto fundraiser
stories.summary: The Newcastle Herald reports young activists protested outside a One Nation fundraiser in the Hunter attended by Pauline Hanson, criticising the party's ideology and calling for venues to refuse bookings.

stories.headline: Passed in: Minns government bins property laws
stories.summary: The Minns government has paused planned underquoting changes for the real estate industry hours before they were due to commence, according to reports across several outlets. The Sydney Morning Herald reports concerns about the laws were raised about a month before the reversal, and The Mandarin reports the pause comes as falling house prices weigh on stamp duty revenue and the state budget.

stories.headline: Emergency volunteers to benefit from greater protections
stories.summary: The Minns government says new laws will give greater employment protections to volunteers who assist during natural disasters and other emergencies.

stories.headline: 'Critical': NSW fast-tracks new Queensland gas pipeline
stories.summary: The Australian reports NSW has declared a proposed direct gas pipeline from Queensland to be critical, and that Pauline Hanson has rejected the PEP11 offshore project.

stories.headline: Thousands of homes and jobs green-lit for Orchard Hills
stories.summary: The government has finalised the Orchard Hills Stage 1 rezoning, which it says will allow up to 5,900 homes and 2,100 jobs around the future Orchard Hills Metro station.

stories.headline: ‘P***ies’: Minister lets rip over crime
stories.summary: News.com.au reports Police Minister Yasmin Catley used a crude term to describe the Liberal opposition's approach to crime during a heated question time exchange, in a report that also deals with the number of prisoners held on remand and near-record NSW inmate numbers.

stories.headline: Dozens of public schools celebrated for NAPLAN improvement under the Minns Labor Government
stories.summary: The government has recognised dozens of public schools for NAPLAN results, attributing improved outcomes to its education reforms.

stories.headline: Hunter mayor to fight developer levy deferral
stories.summary: Cessnock Council says a NSW proposal to defer developer charges could leave a funding shortfall for local roads and parks, the Newcastle Herald reports, with Mayor Daniel Watton raising concerns for regional councils.

stories.headline: ‘They get everything they deserve’: The man who reined in Sydney’s gambling giants
stories.summary: The Sydney Morning Herald profiles Phil Crawford, the state's casino regulator, on his time overseeing the sector.

stories.headline: NSW Premier’s awkward selfie with disgraced ex-mayor
stories.summary: The Australian's Margin Call column reports on a photograph of Premier Chris Minns with former mayor Bill Saravinovski.

stories.headline: Chris Minns’ backflips are adding up. Is he ‘clearing the runway’ or panicking?
stories.summary: The Guardian argues the Premier is accumulating policy reversals — from train timetables to coffee cups and property underquoting — well ahead of the March election, and asks whether this is deliberate pre-election positioning or something less planned.

stories.headline: Minns auctions off his credibility with pause on underquoting laws
stories.summary: In the Sydney Morning Herald, the pause on underquoting rules is characterised as part of a growing pattern of reversals by the NSW government and as damaging to the Premier's credibility.

stories.headline: Dodgy real estate agents are the only winners from Minns’ policy debacle
stories.summary: The Sydney Morning Herald argues the shelved reforms were billed as among the biggest changes to the real estate industry in decades, and that home buyers are the losers from the decision.

stories.headline: “Victoria has its limits”: Why businesses getting a raw deal in Vic should move to Sydney
stories.summary: The Australian carries a business commentary piece arguing Victorian businesses would be better served in Sydney.

elsewhere.text: With under two weeks to the Victorian election, 7NEWS compares Labor, Liberal, Greens and One Nation policies across the major issues.
The AFR argues Victoria's debt burden demands tougher fiscal rules from whoever wins this month's election.
The Tally Room reports the Local Government Change Commission has begun redrawing Brisbane City Council's 26 wards, a reminder of how boundary reviews reshape contests.
Dozens of academics have called for changes to New Zealand's electoral system after what they describe as a distortion in its election result.
